title: The pirate in 3D
summary: The pirate raider is now a 3D model. Your Tripo pirate and rifle are rigged, posed and animated in Blender and rendered from the game's camera into 320 sprites - 8 views each of a 12-frame attack (raising the rifle and firing) and a 28-frame walk cycle, about 25 frames a second - with brighter colours and a rendered ground point under every frame so he stands steady while his legs move. Pirates also fight smarter: shoot one and it turns on you, coming after you if you fired from beyond its reach, and a badly hurt pirate lowers its rifle and runs (you're faster - chase it or let it go). Laser bolts and arrows are now fast and homing, so they can't be dodged. Before the 3D model, the pirate's sheet-cut sprites lost their rifle barrels to the cutter; that's fixed and the cutter kept. The Patcher's code review now shows pictures, sounds and fonts, and Claude can drive Blender directly (Blender Lab's MCP).

steps.title: The pirate, from a 3D model
steps.text: The pirate isn't cut from drawn sheets any more. Your Tripo models (the pirate, already rigged with a 53-bone skeleton, and the rifle) are posed and animated in Blender, then rendered from the game's own camera angle into sprites - every view and frame from the same model, so they all match and nothing gets cropped.

steps.title: The rifle in his hands
steps.text: The rifle hangs from his left hand on an IK chain; from the moment he raises it, his right hand travels onto the fore-grip. This model's arms are short (25 cm shoulder to wrist), so a search found the twist of his torso and right shoulder that lets both hands reach - within 2 cm in every pose - and his head turns back along the barrel.

steps.title: Raising the rifle: 12 frames (was 4)
steps.text: Raising the rifle takes 0.45 s, so it now has 12 frames - about 25 a second - instead of 4. The four poses from your reference frames are the keys; Blender eases between them and interpolates everything in between: the grip, the rifle's angle, the twist, the right hand moving onto the gun. Lowering plays them back over 0.6 s.

diagram.text: eased in and out (smoothstep) between the four key poses

steps.title: A real walk: 28 frames
steps.text: The pirate used to slide along on his idle pose with a little bob. Now he walks: a 28-frame cycle - thighs swinging 18 degrees, knees bending as each foot passes under him, hips dipping on each step, his free arm swinging and the rifle swaying. One cycle covers the game's stride (64 px at 58 px/s: 1.1 s), so his feet keep pace with the ground.

diagram.text: every other frame of the cycle

steps.title: Standing still while the legs move
steps.text: A sprite used to be placed by the middle of its feet - fine standing, but in a walk the feet move, so the figure would jump from frame to frame. Blender now records where the character stands (the point it turns about, on the ground) in every render; that goes into art/pirate/pirate_anchors.json and every frame stands on it.

steps.title: Brighter colours
steps.text: Tripo's textures render pale and pinkish, and the first grade came out dark. The pirate now has a stronger grade in Blender - more saturation and brightness - and a lighter ambient light lifting the shadows on his torso and arms. Three grades were compared at the size he appears in the game.

steps.title: Shoot a pirate and it fights back
steps.text: Every bolt and arrow now knows who fired it, and the one it hits finds out. A pirate turns on whoever shot it at once. Your rifle reaches further than his (700 px against 560), so you used to be able to pick pirates off from beyond their reach - now a pirate hit from out there comes after you, then opens fire. He holds the grudge for 15 s.

diagram.text: chase at 85 px/s  -  grudge 15 s, up to 1600 px
guards and the archer get the same treatment

steps.title: Badly hurt, it runs
steps.text: At 30% of its health or less, a pirate lowers its rifle and runs from the fight, shouting as it goes, steering round water and walls. It's slower than you (120 px/s against your 190), so you can run it down - or let it go. It stops 950 px away (or after 9 s) and lies low there, and while it's hurt it won't pick a fight: come near and it runs again.

diagram.text: rifle down while it runs - no shots; hurt, it avoids any fight

steps.title: Shots you can't dodge
steps.text: Laser bolts - yours, the pirates', the guards' - now fly at 2600 px/s (they were 820-1000) and home in on their target, steering to where it is every frame; the archer's arrows fly at 2200 px/s (were 1150) and home in too. Running or sidestepping doesn't help: fight back, or get out of range before they fire.

steps.title: Nothing cropped
steps.text: Before the 3D pirate, his sprites were cut from your sheets - and the cutter clipped thin rifle barrels, measuring each figure by its pixels per column. It now takes each figure's whole cell, keeps only the figure, and reports anything touching a cell edge; the aimed views went from 137 to 193 px wide. The cutter stays as tools/cut_sheet_views.py for future sheets.

diagram.text: the guard's and the player's sheets checked too: nothing lost

steps.title: The Patcher shows the assets
steps.text: In the code review, files that have no diff are now shown as what they are: pictures full size on a checkerboard (with their pixel and file sizes), sounds with Play / Stop, fonts as sample text, text files as their contents. "All assets" at the top of the list shows every picture of a patch as thumbnails - like the 320 pirate sprites of this one.

review.intro: The pirate raider moves to a 3D model: Blender renders 320 sprites (a 12-frame attack and a 28-frame walk, 8 views each) that SheetPuppet plays by raise and walk phase, standing each on its rendered anchor. Pirates fight back and flee (surface_props.gd), shots carry their shooter and home in, and the Patcher's code review shows assets. The Blender scripts and previews live in external/ (not in builds).

+

+def _ramp(nt, stops, loc):

+def mat_worn(name, colors, metallic, rough, scale=6.0, pits=0.0, bump=0.25, sheen=0.0):
+    """A noisy, worn surface: noise -> colour ramp; pits (voronoi dots) push
+    to the darkest colour; rust (the bright end) is rougher and less metallic."""
+    m, nt, bsdf = _principled(name)
+    tc = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
+    tc.location = (-1100, 0)
+    noise = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+    noise.location = (-900, 100)
+    noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale
+    noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 8.0
+    noise.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.62
+    nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], noise.inputs["Vector"])
+    fac = noise.outputs["Fac"]
+    if pits > 0:
+        vor = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexVoronoi")
+        vor.location = (-900, -200)
+        vor.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale * 5
+        nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], vor.inputs["Vector"])
+        mask = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
+        mask.location = (-700, -200)
+        mask.inputs["From Min"].default_value = 0.0
+        mask.inputs["From Max"].default_value = pits
+        nt.links.new(vor.outputs["Distance"], mask.inputs["Value"])
+        mul = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMath")
+        mul.operation = "MULTIPLY"
+        mul.location = (-500, 0)
+        nt.links.new(fac, mul.inputs[0])
+        nt.links.new(mask.outputs["Result"], mul.inputs[1])
+        fac = mul.outputs["Value"]
+    col = _ramp(nt, colors, (-300, 200))
+    nt.links.new(fac, col.inputs["Fac"])
+    nt.links.new(col.outputs["Color"], bsdf.inputs["Base Color"])
+    rr = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
+    rr.location = (-300, -100)
+    rr.inputs["To Min"].default_value = rough[0]
+    rr.inputs["To Max"].default_value = rough[1]
+    nt.links.new(fac, rr.inputs["Value"])
+    nt.links.new(rr.outputs["Result"], bsdf.inputs["Roughness"])
+    mr = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
+    mr.location = (-300, -300)
+    mr.inputs["To Min"].default_value = metallic[0]
+    mr.inputs["To Max"].default_value = metallic[1]
+    nt.links.new(fac, mr.inputs["Value"])
+    nt.links.new(mr.outputs["Result"], bsdf.inputs["Metallic"])
+    b = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump")
+    b.location = (0, -400)
+    b.inputs["Strength"].default_value = bump
+    b.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.02
+    nt.links.new(fac, b.inputs["Height"])
+    nt.links.new(b.outputs["Normal"], bsdf.inputs["Normal"])
+    if sheen:
+        bsdf.inputs["Sheen Weight"].default_value = sheen
+        bsdf.inputs["Sheen Tint"].default_value = (1.0, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0)
+    return m

+def box(name, size, loc, mats, rot=(0, 0, 0), taper=None, bevel=0.008, rivet_face=None, parent=None):
+    """A bevelled box; taper=(sx, sy) scales the bottom; rivet_face='-y' etc.
+    puts rivets on the corners of that face (material 2)."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1.0)
+    for v in bm.verts:
+        if taper and v.co.z < 0:
+            v.co.x *= taper[0]
+            v.co.y *= taper[1]
+        v.co.x *= size[0]
+        v.co.y *= size[1]
+        v.co.z *= size[2]
+    if rivet_face:
+        ax = "xyz".index(rivet_face[1])
+        sgn = 1 if rivet_face[0] == "+" else -1
+        others = [i for i in range(3) if i != ax]
+        pts = []
+        for a in (-0.38, 0.38):
+            for b in (-0.38, 0.38):
+                p = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
+                p[ax] = sgn * size[ax] * 0.5
+                p[others[0]] = a * size[others[0]]
+                p[others[1]] = b * size[others[1]]
+                pts.append(Vector(p))
+        rivets(bm, pts)
+    ob = _obj_from_bm(name, bm, mats, parent=parent)
+    ob.location = loc
+    ob.rotation_euler = rot
+    if bevel:
+        _bevel(ob, bevel)
+    return ob

+def limb(name, p1, p2, r1, r2, mats, seg=16, squash=1.0, parent=None):

+    d = p2 - p1
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, segments=seg, radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=d.length)
+    for v in bm.verts:
+        v.co.y *= squash
+    ob = _obj_from_bm(name, bm, mats, smooth=True, parent=parent)
+    ob.location = (p1 + p2) * 0.5

+def tattered(name, center, z_top, z_bot, r_top, r_bot, a0, a1, mats, cols=28, rows=9,
+             squash=0.8, rag=0.18, thick=0.012, parent=None):
+    """An open, flaring skirt of cloth around `center` (x, y), from angle a0 to
+    a1 (0 = back (+y), +-pi = front (-y)), its hem torn into points of
+    random length."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    grid = []
+    hem = []
+    for i in range(cols + 1):
+        if i % 2 == 0:
+            hem.append(z_bot - rng.uniform(0.0, rag))          # a point hanging down
+        else:
+            hem.append(z_bot + rng.uniform(0.02, rag * 0.9))    # a tear up into the cloth
+    for j in range(rows + 1):
+        t = j / rows
+        row = []
+        for i in range(cols + 1):
+            a = a0 + (a1 - a0) * i / cols
+            zb = hem[i]
+            z = z_top + (zb - z_top) * t
+            r = r_top + (r_bot - r_top) * t ** 1.3
+            wav = 0.012 * math.sin(i * 1.7 + j * 0.6) * t
+            row.append(bm.verts.new((center[0] + (r + wav) * math.sin(a),
+                                     center[1] + (r + wav) * math.cos(a) * squash, z)))
+        grid.append(row)
+    for j in range(rows):
+        for i in range(cols):
+            bm.faces.new((grid[j][i], grid[j][i + 1], grid[j + 1][i + 1], grid[j + 1][i]))
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    ob = _obj_from_bm(name, bm, mats, smooth=True, parent=parent)
+    s = ob.modifiers.new("Solidify", "SOLIDIFY")
+    s.thickness = thick
+    s.offset = 1.0
+    return ob

+    cu.bevel_resolution = 4
+    cu.resolution_u = 10
+    sp = cu.splines.new("NURBS")
+    sp.points.add(len(pts) - 1)
+    for k, p in enumerate(pts):
+        sp.points[k].co = (*p, 1.0)
+        sp.points[k].radius = max(0.08, 1.0 - k / (len(pts) - 1)) ** 0.8
+    sp.order_u = 4
+    sp.use_endpoint_u = True
+    for m in mats:
+        cu.materials.append(m)
+    return _link(name, cu, parent)

@@ -1,0 +1,461 @@ 
+"""The pirate NPC's sprites, rendered from the Tripo models.
+
+Sources (external/blender/pirate/source/): pirate.glb (rigged by Tripo with a
+Mixamo skeleton, T-pose, facing -Y, 0.96 m tall) and gun.glb (muzzle at -X).
+The scene: external/blender/pirate.blend.
+
+  setup()          import both (if not in the scene yet), put the gun in the
+                   LEFT hand: the gun hangs under the empty "GunCtrl" (its
+                   origin = the grip, local -Y = the muzzle, +Z = the top);
+                   IK on both forearms - the left hand to the grip, the right
+                   hand to "HandR_Goal" (blended from its rest onto the fore-grip).
+  POSES            the four key poses of the attack (from the reference frames
+                   external/images/npc_pirate_frame_*): rifle hanging at the
+                   side, across the body, at the hip, aimed.
+  apply_pose(f)    an attack frame (ATTACK: idle, raise1..raise10, aim - 12
+                   frames interpolated through the four key POSES, eased).
+  apply_walk(k)    frame k of the in-place walk cycle (WALK_N = 28 frames, the
+                   rifle hanging in the left hand).
+  keyframe_all()   both as actions: PirateAttack (assigned) and PirateWalk, 25 fps.
+  render_all(dir)  8 directions x FRAMES (12 attack + 28 walk) ->
+                   dir/<frame>_<dir>.png, from the game's view (orthographic,
+                   30 degrees above).
+
+Run inside Blender (MCP execute, or blender -b pirate_rig.blend --python ...).
+The PNGs are cropped / scaled into art/pirate/ by tools/sprites_from_renders.py.
+"""
+import json
+import math
+import os
+
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+HERE = "/home/kilon/MEGA/Dimitris/godot/space-atrapos/external/blender/pirate/"
+SRC = HERE + "source/"
+P = "mixamorig:"
+GUN_LEN = 0.5                       # the rifle's length (m) - the pirate is 0.96 m
+GRIP = Vector((0.25, 0.0, 0.12))    # on gun.glb: the pistol grip (under the hand)
+FORE = Vector((-0.02, 0.0, 0.15))   # ... and under the barrel, for the other hand
+DIRS = ["e", "se", "s", "sw", "w", "nw", "n", "ne"]
+
+
+def _norm(v):
+    return Vector(v).normalized()
+
+
+def _frame(pos, fwd, up):
+    """A matrix with origin pos, local -Y along fwd (the muzzle), +Z ~ up."""
+    y = -_norm(fwd)
+    z = _norm(up)
+    x = y.cross(z).normalized()
+    z = x.cross(y).normalized()
+    m = Matrix((x, y, z)).transposed().to_4x4()
+    m.translation = Vector(pos)
+    return m
+
+
+# Per pose: the grip (world, character facing -Y, left = +X), the muzzle
+# direction, the gun's top, whether the right hand holds the gun, and the free
+# right arm's rotation (idle). Spine twist / lean in radians.
+POSES = {
+    "idle":   dict(grip=(0.205, -0.02, 0.5), fwd=(0.05, -0.3, -1.0), up=(0.0, -1.0, 0.3), right=0.0,
+                   twist=0.0, lean=0.0),
+    # (twist / clav found by a search so both hands reach: the arms are short)
+    "raise1": dict(grip=(0.07, -0.10, 0.52), fwd=(-0.65, -0.55, -0.45), up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), right=1.0,
+                   twist=0.55, clav=0.4, lean=0.05),
+    "raise2": dict(grip=(0.05, -0.13, 0.55), fwd=(-0.2, -1.0, -0.22), up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), right=1.0,
+                   twist=0.55, clav=0.4, lean=0.08),
+    "aim":    dict(grip=(0.06, -0.16, 0.63), fwd=(-0.08, -1.0, 0.0), up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), right=1.0,
+                   twist=0.55, clav=0.4, lean=0.1),
+}
+
+
+def _obj(name):
+    return bpy.data.objects.get(name)
+
+
+def _empty(name, parent, size=0.03):
+    e = _obj(name)
+    if e is None:
+        e = bpy.data.objects.new(name, None)
+        bpy.data.collections["Pirate"].objects.link(e)
+    e.empty_display_size = size
+    e.parent = parent
+    e.matrix_parent_inverse = Matrix.Identity(4)
+    return e
+
+
+def pirate_mesh():
+    return [o for o in bpy.data.collections["Pirate"].objects if o.type == "MESH" and o.name.startswith("tripo")][0]
+
+
+def gun_mesh():
+    return [o for o in bpy.data.collections["Gun"].objects if o.type == "MESH"][0]
+
+
+def _import(name):
+    coll = bpy.data.collections.get(name.capitalize())
+    if coll and coll.objects:
+        return
+    coll = coll or bpy.data.collections.new(name.capitalize())
+    if coll.name not in bpy.context.scene.collection.children:
+        bpy.context.scene.collection.children.link(coll)
+    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
+    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=SRC + name + ".glb")
+    for o in [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o not in before]:
+        for c in list(o.users_collection):
+            c.objects.unlink(o)
+        coll.objects.link(o)
+
+
+def setup():
+    _import("pirate")
+    _import("gun")
+    ico = _obj("Icosphere")              # (the bones' display shape)
+    if ico:
+        ico.hide_render = ico.hide_viewport = True
+    arm = _obj("Armature")
+    root = _obj("Node_0")
+    # The gun: scaled, turned so the muzzle is local -Y, the grip at GunCtrl.
+    ctrl = _empty("GunCtrl", root, 0.06)
+    g = gun_mesh()
+    k = GUN_LEN / g.dimensions.x if g.parent is None else g.get("pir_k", 1.0)
+    g["pir_k"] = k
+    rot = Matrix.Rotation(math.pi / 2, 4, "Z")             # -X (muzzle) -> -Y
+    g.parent = ctrl
+    g.matrix_parent_inverse = Matrix.Identity(4)
+    g.matrix_basis = Matrix.Translation(-(rot @ (GRIP * k))) @ rot @ Matrix.Scale(k, 4)
+    # IK targets on the gun, poles behind / outside the elbows.
+    tl = _empty("IK_HandL", ctrl)
+    tl.location = (0, 0, 0)
+    tr = _empty("IK_HandR", ctrl)
+    tr.location = rot @ ((FORE - GRIP) * k)
+    # The right hand's IK goal: blended between its rest at the side and the
+    # fore-grip (IK_HandR, on the gun) - so it travels smoothly onto the gun.
+    goal = _empty("HandR_Goal", root)
+    old = _obj("Rest_R")                   # (before: a second IK switched on and off)
+    if old:
+        bpy.data.objects.remove(old, do_unlink=True)
+    pl = _empty("Pole_L", root)
+    pl.location = (0.45, 0.35, 0.55)
+    prr = _empty("Pole_R", root)
+    prr.location = (-0.45, 0.35, 0.55)
+    for side, tgt, pole in (("Left", tl, pl), ("Right", goal, prr)):
+        pb = arm.pose.bones[P + side + "ForeArm"]
+        c = pb.constraints.get("IK") or pb.constraints.new("IK")
+        c.target = tgt
+        c.pole_target = pole
+        c.pole_angle = math.radians(-90 if side == "Left" else -90)
+        c.chain_count = 2
+        c.use_tail = True
+        c.influence = 1.0
+    pb = arm.pose.bones[P + "RightForeArm"]
+    if pb.constraints.get("IK_rest"):
+        pb.constraints.remove(pb.constraints["IK_rest"])
+    for a in ("PirateWalkHand",):
+        if bpy.data.actions.get(a):
+            bpy.data.actions.remove(bpy.data.actions[a])
+    # (brighter and more saturated than the raw textures - the user found 0.85 / 1.1 too dark)
+    grade(pirate_mesh().data.materials[0], sat=1.45, val=1.1, contrast=0.06, hue=0.515)
+    grade(gun_mesh().data.materials[0], sat=1.35, val=1.05, contrast=0.08)
+    stage()
+    return {"gun_scale": round(k, 3)}
+
+
+# The attack: ATTACK_N frames from idle to aim (idle, raise1 .. raise<N-2>, aim),
+# the key poses above at 0, 1/3, 2/3 and 1 of the way, eased in and out;
+# in between everything is interpolated - the grip, the rifle's direction, the
+# right hand travelling from the side onto the fore-grip, the twist.
+# The game plays them over RAISE_TIME (0.45 s): 12 frames ~ 25 fps.
+ATTACK_N = 12
+_KEYS = ("idle", "raise1", "raise2", "aim")
+ATTACK = tuple(["idle"] + ["raise%d" % k for k in range(1, ATTACK_N - 1)] + ["aim"])
+
+
+def attack_params(t):
+    """The pose t of the way (0 idle .. 1 aimed) through the attack."""
+    t = t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)                      # (ease in and out)
+    x = t * (len(_KEYS) - 1)
+    i = min(int(x), len(_KEYS) - 2)
+    u = x - i
+    a, b = POSES[_KEYS[i]], POSES[_KEYS[i + 1]]
+    out = {}
+    for key in ("grip", "fwd", "up"):
+        va, vb = Vector(a[key]), Vector(b[key])
+        if key != "grip":
+            va, vb = va.normalized(), vb.normalized()
+        out[key] = va.lerp(vb, u)
+    for key in ("right", "twist", "lean", "clav"):
+        out[key] = a.get(key, 0.0) * (1 - u) + b.get(key, 0.0) * u
+    return out
+
+
+def apply_pose(name):
+    """One of the attack frames (ATTACK), or one of the key POSES."""
+    if name in ATTACK:
+        apply_params(attack_params(ATTACK.index(name) / (ATTACK_N - 1)))
+    else:
+        apply_params(POSES[name])
+
+
+def apply_params(p, rest=None):
+    """Poses the rig: the rifle (grip / fwd / up), the right hand `right` of the
+    way from its rest (`rest`, default REST_R) onto the fore-grip, the spine
+    twist / lean, the right collarbone and the neck."""
+    arm = _obj("Armature")
+    ctrl = _obj("GunCtrl")
+    root = _obj("Node_0")

+    cl = arm.pose.bones[P + "RightShoulder"]

+    cl.rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, -p.get("clav", 0.0))

+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ walking
+# An in-place walk cycle of WALK_N frames (walk1..walkN), the rifle hanging in
+# the left hand as in idle. One cycle = two steps = the game's STRIDE (64 px,
+# about 0.52 m for this 1 m tall figure on screen): the thighs swing +-WALK_SWING,
+# the knee bends in the swing, the foot stays about level, the hips dip on the
+# contacts, the free right arm swings against the legs, the rifle sways.
+# Axes (found by probing the rig): thigh / knee / foot all turn on local Z -
+# thigh -Z = forward, knee +Z = bend, foot +Z = toes down; hips local +Y = up.

+WALK_SWING = 0.32          # rad, the thighs (about 18 deg)
+WALK_KNEE = 0.55           # rad, the knee in the swing
+WALK_BOB = 0.012           # m, the hips' rise and fall
+LEG_BONES = ("LeftUpLeg", "LeftLeg", "LeftFoot", "RightUpLeg", "RightLeg", "RightFoot")
+REST_R = (-0.2, 0.0, 0.47)
+
+
+def apply_walk(k):
+    """Frame k (0..WALK_N-1) of the walk cycle."""
+    w = 2 * math.pi * k / WALK_N

+    # against the right leg (forward with the left leg).
+    p = dict(POSES["idle"])
+    p["grip"] = Vector(p["grip"]) + Vector((0.0, 0.03 * math.sin(w), WALK_BOB * math.cos(2 * w)))
+    p["fwd"] = Vector(p["fwd"]) + Vector((0.0, -0.12 * math.sin(w), 0.0))
+    rx, ry, rz = REST_R
+    apply_params(p, rest=(rx, ry - 0.07 * math.sin(w), rz + 0.015 * (1 - math.cos(2 * w))))
+    arm = _obj("Armature")
+    for side, ph in (("Left", 0.0), ("Right", math.pi)):
+        fwd = WALK_SWING * math.sin(w + ph)                      # the thigh forward (+) / back (-)

+        arm.pose.bones[P + side + "Leg"].rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, knee)
+        arm.pose.bones[P + side + "Foot"].rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, foot)
+    arm.pose.bones[P + "Hips"].location = (0.0, WALK_BOB * math.cos(2 * w), 0.0)
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()

+FRAMES = ATTACK + tuple("walk%d" % (k + 1) for k in range(WALK_N))

+def grade(mat, sat, val, contrast, hue=0.5):

+        hsv.name = "SPR_GradeHSV"
+        bc = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBrightContrast")
+        bc.name = "SPR_GradeBC"
+        nt.links.new(src, hsv.inputs["Color"])
+        nt.links.new(hsv.outputs["Color"], bc.inputs["Color"])
+        nt.links.new(bc.outputs["Color"], bsdf.inputs["Base Color"])

+    hsv.inputs["Saturation"].default_value = sat
+    hsv.inputs["Value"].default_value = val

+def _bake(names, count, pose_fn, bones, legs=False):
+    """Keyframes frames 1..count (pose_fn(k) poses frame k) into new actions
+    names = {object name: action name}; the actions assigned before stay."""
+    arm, ctrl, goal = _obj("Armature"), _obj("GunCtrl"), _obj("HandR_Goal")
+    obs = (arm, ctrl, goal)
+    keep = {}
+    for ob in obs:

+        old = bpy.data.actions.get(names[ob.name])

+def keyframe_all():

+    the walk (WALK_N frames) as PirateWalk / -Gun / -Hand (switch to them in

+def _linear(act):
+    """Straight from frame to frame (every frame is a rendered pose)."""

+    # anchor (tools/sprites_from_renders.py -> art/<id>/<id>_anchors.json).

hunks.note: setup(): import, rifle under GunCtrl (origin = the grip), IK on both forearms (the right hand's goal blended from its rest onto the fore-grip), colour grade, lights and camera. attack_params(t): the key poses interpolated and eased. apply_walk(k): thighs +-18 deg, knee bend in the swing, level feet, hip dip, arm swing, rifle sway. keyframe_all(): PirateAttack / PirateWalk at 25 fps. render_all(): 8 views x FRAMES and renders/meta.json (the ground point).

bubbles.text: The right hand follows this empty (IK). Moving it between the hand's rest spot and the rifle's fore-grip is how the pirate brings its other hand up to the gun.
The 12 attack frames are in-betweens of 4 hand-made key poses (idle, raise1, raise2, aim), eased with a smoothstep so the raise starts and ends gently.
"right" 0..1: how far the free hand has travelled from its rest to the fore-grip.
The knee only bends in the swing phase, a little after the thigh starts forward - that delay keeps the foot from flicking up.
Keeps the sole level with the ground by undoing the thigh and knee angles, then tips the toes down as the foot lifts off.
An orthographic camera 30 deg above the ground - the game's isometric view, so the sprites match the world.
Instead of moving the camera, the pirate is turned to each of the 8 directions.
Where the pirate's feet meet the ground in every render: the anchor that keeps the sprites from jittering in the game.

+Writes <out_dir>/<prefix>_<angle>.png for 315 0 45 90 / 135 180 225 270 at the
+sheet's size. Each figure gets a whole cell (up to its neighbours' middles),
+so thin parts - a rifle barrel - aren't cut off; only the figure and pieces
+inside its outline are kept (not neighbours, labels or the legend). It prints
+TOUCHES <angle> <side> if a figure reaches its cell's edge (check it by eye).
+Then scale / mirror / name the views for the game (see the pirate in
+external/patcher/history and art/pirate/).
+"""
+import sys, json
+from collections import deque
+from PIL import Image, ImageFilter
+import numpy as np
+src, out, prefix = sys.argv[1:4]
+im = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
+H, W = im.shape[:2]
+# The backdrop: the most common colour of the area between the two rows of figures.
+band = im[455:475, 150:1500].reshape(-1, 3)
+vals, counts = np.unique((band // 2) * 2, axis=0, return_counts=True)
+BG = vals[counts.argmax()] + 1
+d = np.abs(im - BG).sum(2)
+mask = d > 55
+# Two rows of figures (labels below each).
+cells = []
+for (y0, y1) in [(0, 445), (465, 925)]:
+    cols = mask[y0:y1].sum(0)
+    runs = []; on = False
+    for x, c in enumerate(cols):
+        if c > 25 and not on: s = x; on = True
+        if c <= 25 and on: runs.append((s, x)); on = False
+    if on: runs.append((s, W))
+    runs = [r for r in runs if r[1] - r[0] > 60 and r[0] > 140 and r[1] < W - 40]
+    # merge runs separated by small gaps (a rifle barrel etc.)
+    merged = []
+    for r in runs:
+        if merged and r[0] - merged[-1][1] < 25: merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], r[1])
+        else: merged.append(r)
+    merged = sorted(merged, key=lambda r: -(r[1] - r[0]))[:4]
+    merged.sort()
+    # Whole cells: borders halfway between neighbouring figures (a thin rifle
+    # barrel has too few pixels per column to be found by counting them).
+    centres = [(r[0] + r[1]) / 2 for r in merged]
+    for k, r in enumerate(merged):
+        left = int(centres[k - 1] + 30) if k > 0 else max(0, int(centres[0] - 300))
+        right = int(centres[k + 1] - 30) if k < 3 else min(W - 30, int(centres[3] + 300))
+        cells.append((left, right, y0, min(H, y1 + 15)))
+assert len(cells) == 8, cells
+ANG = [315, 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270]
+DIRS = {0: "s", 45: "sw", 90: "w", 135: "ne", 180: "n", 225: "nw", 270: "e", 315: "se"}
+STEP, LUM, SAT = 6, 120, 26
+for ang, (x0, x1, y0, y1) in zip(ANG, cells):
+    c = im[y0:y1, x0:x1]; h, w = c.shape[:2]
+    dist = np.abs(c - BG).sum(2); lum = c.sum(2); sat = c.max(2) - c.min(2)
+    bglike = dist < 12
+    seen = np.zeros((h, w), bool)
+    q = deque()
+    for y in range(h):
+        for x in (0, w - 1):
+            if bglike[y, x]: seen[y, x] = True; q.append((y, x))
+    for x in range(w):
+        for y in (0, h - 1):
+            if bglike[y, x] and not seen[y, x]: seen[y, x] = True; q.append((y, x))
+    while q:
+        y, x = q.popleft()
+        for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
+            ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
+            if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and not seen[ny, nx]:
+                ok = bglike[ny, nx] or (np.abs(c[ny, nx] - c[y, x]).sum() <= STEP and lum[ny, nx] < LUM and sat[ny, nx] < SAT)
+                if ok: seen[ny, nx] = True; q.append((ny, nx))
+    alpha = np.where(seen, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
+    # Keep the figure: its biggest piece, plus any piece lying within its outline
+    # (a barrel tip separated by a gap) - not neighbours' parts, the legend or labels.
+    from collections import deque as _dq
+    on = alpha > 0
+    lab = np.zeros((h, w), np.int32); comps = []
+    for y in range(h):
+        for x in range(w):
+            if on[y, x] and not lab[y, x]:
+                cid = len(comps) + 1; q = _dq([(y, x)]); lab[y, x] = cid; n = 0
+                y0c, y1c, x0c, x1c = y, y, x, x
+                while q:
+                    cy, cx = q.popleft(); n += 1
+                    y0c = min(y0c, cy); y1c = max(y1c, cy); x0c = min(x0c, cx); x1c = max(x1c, cx)
+                    for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
+                        ny, nx = cy + dy, cx + dx
+                        if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and on[ny, nx] and not lab[ny, nx]:
+                            lab[ny, nx] = cid; q.append((ny, nx))
+                comps.append((n, y0c, y1c, x0c, x1c))
+    main = max(range(len(comps)), key=lambda i: comps[i][0])
+    _, my0, my1, mx0, mx1 = comps[main]
+    keep = np.zeros(len(comps) + 1, bool)
+    for i, (n, a0, a1, b0, b1) in enumerate(comps):
+        if i == main or (n > 30 and a0 >= my0 - 20 and a1 <= my1 and b0 >= mx0 - 40 and b1 <= mx1 + 40):
+            keep[i + 1] = True
+    alpha = np.where(keep[lab], 255, 0).astype(np.uint8)
+    edge = []
+    if alpha[:, :2].max() > 0: edge.append("left")
+    if alpha[:, -2:].max() > 0: edge.append("right")
+    if alpha[:2, :].max() > 0: edge.append("top")
+    if edge: print("  TOUCHES", ang, edge)
+    a = Image.fromarray(alpha).filter(ImageFilter.MinFilter(3)).filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(0.7))
+    rgba = Image.fromarray(c.astype(np.uint8)).convert('RGBA'); rgba.putalpha(a)
+    rgba = rgba.crop(rgba.getbbox())
+    rgba.save('%s/%s_%d.png' % (out, prefix, ang))
+print("bg", BG, "cells", cells)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Turns Blender renders of a character (<renders>/<frame>_<dir>.png, all from
+the same orthographic camera, transparent background) into the game's sprites
+art/<id>/<id>_<frame>_<dir>.png (SheetPuppet's 8 views per frame).
+
+Every picture is cropped to what's opaque (plus a margin) and scaled by ONE
+factor, the one that makes idle_s `--height` pixels tall - so all the frames
+keep the same size.
+
+If the renders come with meta.json ({"ground": [x, y]} - where the character
+stands, the point it turns about, in render pixels; pirate_sprites.py writes
+it), every sprite's anchor (that point, in the sprite) goes into
+art/<id>/<id>_anchors.json {"<frame>_<dir>": [x, y]}: SheetPuppet stands the
+sprite on it - steady through a walk cycle, whatever the feet are doing.
+
+  python3 tools/sprites_from_renders.py <renders dir> <id> [--height 258]
+
+e.g. external/blender/pirate/renders -> art/pirate/ (pirate_sprites.py renders them).
+"""
+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+
+from PIL import Image
+
+PAD = 3
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("renders")
+    ap.add_argument("id")
+    ap.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=258)
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(a.renders, "*_*.png")))
+    if not files:
+        raise SystemExit("no renders in " + a.renders)
+    meta_path = os.path.join(a.renders, "meta.json")
+    ground = json.load(open(meta_path))["ground"] if os.path.exists(meta_path) else None
+    ref = Image.open(os.path.join(a.renders, "idle_s.png")).convert("RGBA")
+    l, t, r, b = ref.getchannel("A").point(lambda v: 255 if v > 8 else 0).getbbox()
+    k = a.height / float(b - t)
+    out_dir = os.path.join("art", a.id)
+    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    anchors = {}
+    for f in files:
+        name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0]       # <frame>_<dir>
+        im = Image.open(f).convert("RGBA")
+        bb = im.getchannel("A").point(lambda v: 255 if v > 8 else 0).getbbox()
+        if bb is None:
+            print("  (empty)", name)
+            continue
+        l, t, r, b = bb
+        box = (max(0, l - PAD), max(0, t - PAD), min(im.width, r + PAD), min(im.height, b + PAD))
+        im = im.crop(box)
+        size = (max(1, round(im.width * k)), max(1, round(im.height * k)))
+        # (resized premultiplied, so the edges don't pick up the black background)
+        im = im.convert("RGBa").resize(size, Image.LANCZOS).convert("RGBA")
+        dst = os.path.join(out_dir, "%s_%s.png" % (a.id, name))
+        im.save(dst, optimize=True)
+        if ground:
+            anchors[name] = [round((ground[0] - box[0]) * k, 1), round((ground[1] - box[1]) * k, 1)]
+        print("  %-28s %dx%d" % (dst, size[0], size[1]))
+    if anchors:
+        with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "%s_anchors.json" % a.id), "w") as fh:
+            json.dump(anchors, fh, indent=0, sort_keys=True)
+    print("scale %.3f, %d sprites%s" % (k, len(files), ", anchors" if anchors else ""))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
